source_title: Haydale Graphene Industries Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 36 and 68 state that the financial statements were approved and authorised for issue by the Board on 14 December 2021; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: COVID-19 subdued aerospace demand and commercial revenue was broadly flat at £2.90m. Gross margin eased to 68% from 70%, although adjusted operating loss improved to £2.17m from £2.54m. Cash increased to £1.64m from £0.82m, but operating activities still used £1.19m, borrowings rose to £1.73m and the US working-capital facility was fully utilised. The group reduced headcount and its operating cost base while reporting commercial progress and completing a post-period £5.10m equity raise.
already_announced_exclusion: The headcount reduction, cost-base realignment, premises subletting, furlough and support schemes, product or market diversification, capacity investments and September 2021 equity fundraising were disclosed or completed before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Persistent losses, cash consumption, increased borrowings and a fully utilised facility create strong pressure despite improving losses and cash. Commercial progress and the completed equity raise provide meaningful but limited contrary evidence.

source_title: Haydale Graphene Industries Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 28 and 61 state that the financial statements were approved and authorised for issue by the Board on 25 October 2023; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 48.3% to £4.30m, but gross margin fell to 56% from 60%, adjusted operating loss widened to £3.49m and the statutory loss increased to £6.17m. Operating activities used £3.66m, cash was only £1.38m and borrowings were £1.37m. Management's going-concern work included revenue, cost and funding sensitivities; a £5.1m post-period equity raise was principally for working capital. US demand recovered and new commercial partnerships supported growth expectations.
already_announced_exclusion: The focus on core offerings, planned resource investment, cost savings already reflected in forecasts, asset impairment, product or market initiatives, September 2022 financing and the October 2023 £5.1m equity fundraising were disclosed or completed before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Rapid revenue growth is outweighed by a widening loss, material operating cash burn, thin cash resources and explicit funding sensitivity. Recovery, partnerships and the completed working-capital raise provide moderate contrary evidence.

source_title: HSS Hire Group Annual Report and Financial Statements 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 45, 72 and 81 state that the strategic report, directors' report and financial statements were approved or authorised by the Board on 27 April 2022; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose to £303.3m from £250.1m, adjusted EBITDA to £69.8m from £59.6m and adjusted EBITA to £31.7m from £13.4m as performance recovered above pre-COVID levels through a lower-cost model. Strategic disposals and cash generation materially strengthened the balance sheet, reduced leverage and supported refinancing. The group described its 2017 delevering, Tool Hire transformation and commercial-strengthening plan as complete and entered 2022 with strong trading momentum.
already_announced_exclusion: The organisational and network restructures, property exits, disposals, refinancing, deleveraging, lower-cost operating model and completed 2017 transformation programme were disclosed or completed before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Residual pandemic and market risks warrant limited pressure only. Strong growth, sharply improved profitability, deleveraging, refinancing and the declared completion of the prior transformation provide very strong contrary evidence.

source_title: HSS Hire Group Annual Report and Financial Statements 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 52, 70 and 82 state that the strategic report, directors' report and financial statements were approved or authorised by the Board on 30 April 2024; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue grew 4.9% to £349.1m despite a challenging market, but adjusted EBITDA fell to £65.1m from £71.6m and margin to 18.7% from 21.5%; adjusted profit before tax fell to £11.9m from £21.0m. Net operating cash fell to £20.2m from £39.0m, net debt rose to £111.6m and leverage to 1.7x, while liquidity remained £68.2m. Demand softened in some segments amid inflation and higher interest costs. The group accelerated its already-disclosed move from branches to builders merchants and retained a strong balance sheet and positive growth positioning.
already_announced_exclusion: The divisional and legal restructuring, branch-to-builders-merchant migration, closures approved by March 2024, Power-business disposal, debt repayment, central-sales changes, technology investment and other disclosed strategic actions were public or completed before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Falling profit and margins, softer demand, lower cash generation and rising leverage create meaningful pressure. Continued revenue growth, substantial liquidity, positive returns and management's strong-balance-sheet assessment provide material contrary evidence.
